extracted.intended_audience: students, instructors, and readers of Rudin's Principles of Mathematical Analysis (3rd ed.)
extracted.subtask_description: A collected list of errata and addenda for Chapters 1–7 of Walter Rudin's Principles of Mathematical Analysis, 3rd Edition, giving precise textual, notational, hypothesis, and proof corrections and suggestions for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.description: Change this line to ‘‘(ii)’’.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.4, Definition 1.10 clearer statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A clearer statement would be, ‘‘Every subset E ⊂ S which is nonempty and bounded above has a supremum sup E in S.’’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace/improve the original wording of Definition 1.10 with the clearer phrasing that explicitly requires nonempty and bounded above.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.5, last 5 lines of proof of Theorem 1.11
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the last five lines of the proof with corrected text: If γ ∈ S is an upper bound of E, then γ ≥ α’’ for greater clarity. If α were not a lower bound of B, there would be some x ∈ B satisfying x < α. This x would be an upper bound of L (by the preceding paragraph), contradicting our assumption that α is the least upper bound of L. So α is a lower bound of B. Now if y is any lower bound of B, y ≤ sup L = α;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this corrected chain of inequalities/logic to fix the argument's clarity and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct the typographical error in the text to preserve readability and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.6, Proposition 1.14 addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the sentence: 'this shows that α is the greatest lower bound of B.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment Proposition 1.14's argument with this concluding remark to clarify the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebraic identity note
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the identity (e) – (x+y) = (– x) + (– y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either discuss this in class or make it an exercise — note asks 'Can you see how to prove this?'

rubrics_metrics.name: P.12, extended real number conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the convention that x + (+∞) and x + (–∞) may be abbreviated x + ∞ and x – ∞ respectively, and that addition and multiplication are commutative on the extended reals so definitions imply cases like +∞ + x = +∞. Also, the three equations in (a) should have the respective conditions 'If x is real or +∞', 'If x is real or –∞', and in the last case simply 'If x is real'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state these conventions in the definitions involving extended real numbers to avoid ambiguity about cases and commutativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.16, Theorem 1.37 addendum
rubrics_metrics.description: Add one more part: (g) Assuming k > 0, there exists a vector u with |u| = 1 such that u · x = |x|. If x ≠ 0 let u = |x|^{-1} x; if x = 0 let u be any vector with |u| = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this constructive part to supply a vector achieving the norm via inner product, helpful in later proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid circular reasoning when invoking Archimedean property
rubrics_metrics.description: P.19: The author refers to the Archimedean property of Q as a consequence of Theorem 1.20(a); this is circular. The Archimedean property of Q is elementary: given x, y ∈ Q with x > 0, write y/x as a fraction with positive denominator and pick any integer n greater than its numerator to find n > y/x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not deduce Archimedean property from results that implicitly use it; instead give the direct elementary argument for Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.29, after display (17) phrasing correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Change 'Hence there is a subset' to 'Hence we cannot say that the map sending the natural number n to the nth term of this sequence is a one-to-one correspondence; but clearly there is a subset'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend the sentence to avoid an incorrect implication and to make precise what can be said about correspondence and subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.31, Definition 2.17 a/b clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rudin doesn't say whether a and b are real numbers or extended real numbers. The definition of 'segment' should contain the assumption 'a < b' (otherwise the empty set would be a segment); 'interval' should contain 'a ≤ b'. In exercises (e.g., p.45 exercise 29) one must understand them as extended real numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit whether endpoints are real or extended real and include inequalities assumptions in definitions to avoid unintended empty sets and ensure consistency with later uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.35, Proof of Theorem 2.27(a) correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the text to: 'We must show that any limit point p of E lies in E. Now any neighborhood N of p contains some q ∈ E. Since N is open, N contains some neighborhood M of q, so every neighborhood N of p contains a point r ∈ E, so p ∈ E.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this corrected local neighborhood argument to properly show limit points belong to E.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.36, topology explanatory addendum
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a discussion explaining that Chapter 2 is about metric spaces and 'topology' refers to the family T of open sets; give the definition of topological space (X,T) with conditions (i) unions arbitrary, (ii) finite intersections, (iii) ∅ and X in T. Explain closed sets, limit points, interior, compactness in terms of open sets; note neighborhood and bounded subset are metric-space-specific notions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide this explanatory material to situate Rudin's material within general topology and clarify terminology (neighborhood vs open ball) and motivations for studying general topological spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.36, end of Definition 2.31 subcover phrase

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the definition of subcover to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the supplied corrected recursive construction to fix the argument in the proof (full display provided in errata).
